title: Attenuated regional traffic orchestration for stream-concurrency safe failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement an active-active regional traffic orchestrator that performs fine-grained, attenuated traffic shifts for streaming and sessionful requests while preserving SLOs and avoiding mass reconnects. Motivation: our current coarse-grained regional cutover creates spikes of reconnects and KV cache churn for long-lived streaming sessions, which leads to token latency regressions and elevated error rates during failovers. This ticket designs and prototypes a traffic attenuation + staged-circuit approach that minimizes session loss and keeps tail latencies within SLOs during regional degradation or capacity events.

Scope and constraints: only affects hosted API edge/gateway routing layer; behaviour must be configurable per-customer and per-route; must interoperate with existing KV-cache sync mechanism (ENG-14257) and per-request routing logic (ENG-33122). Target SLOs: 99.9% availability for short requests, and 99.0% continuity for streaming sessions during single-region impairment windows. Aim to keep p99 additional token latency < 150ms during controlled traffic attenuations.

Design summary: 1) Attenuated traffic shift: instead of abrupt drain, perform progressive traffic handoffs in fractional steps (e.g., 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) using weighted routing for new connections and a sticky token for existing streams. 2) Session-aware steering: maintain a session affinity map (hashed session-id -> region/edge) with TTL and soft-handover hooks; only migrate sessions when the target has warmed KV state or after explicit client reconnect window. 3) Stream-safe handshake: extend our streaming handshake so that when a session is marked for relocation we send a SWITCH_NOTICE event to the client with optional resume token; clients that support resume can reconnect transparently. 4) Circuit-breaking tiers: implement a three-tiered circuit for each region: open/attenuate/hard-close. Open = normal; Attenuate = begin fractional shift and enable load-shedding of long-tail requests; Hard-close = route new requests away and refuse non-resumeable streams. 5) Load-shedding policy: prioritize short interactive GRPC/text completions and system-critical routes; apply probabilistic shed for best-effort batch-like requests. 6) KV cache warming and verification: the orchestrator triggers KV sync prefetch for candidate target nodes before increasing weight; check pre-warm success metric (cache-hit > X) before next step.

Telemetry and observability: add per-step metrics (shift_step, step_duration, prewarm_success, session_migrations, resume_rate), circuit state transitions, and streaming failure annotations. Import existing trace spans for handshake and KV sync to Sentry/Tempo; dashboards for each region showing weighted traffic, retry rates, and token-latency deltas.

Rollout plan: a) Canary: implement feature-flagged rollout to internal beta with 0.5% of traffic for 48h; b) Ramp: increase to 5% for controlled experiments and run chaos-simulated region degrade tests; c) Customer opt-in: target self-serve toggle in Console under rollout controls; d) Default: enable for all hosted traffic after 4-week observation window and postmortem review.

Acceptance criteria: - No more than 1.5x increase in p99 token latency during a controlled attenuation for canary customers. - Successful resume rate >= 95% for resume-capable clients during a staged failover. - Metric thresholds for prewarm success and session-migration fallbacks have alerting rules and runbooks. - Documented Console controls and rollout knobs.

Implementation notes: prototype the orchestrator as a new control-plane controller service that talks to the gateway routing table via gRPC. The controller computes per-region weights and emits step plans. Gateways must expose a small API to accept plan steps and report local readiness. We'll reuse existing KV-sync endpoints and extend the handshake protocol for SWITCH_NOTICE + resume_token.

Risk and mitigations: the most likely failure mode is premature migration leading to cache-miss storms; mitigation is conservative prewarm checks and circuit-backoff with exponential hold times. Another risk is client incompatibility with SWITCH_NOTICE; mitigated by transparent fallback to connection-proxying for non-resumeable sessions and feature-flagging.

Next steps: finalize protocol spec, implement controller scaffold, add gateway readiness API, implement traffic-weighting algorithm, and write load tests and chaos scenarios.
